Tesla Just Gained 13% in a Month: Take Profits, or Buy More? ©DOD photo and SUMALI IBNU CHAMID from Alemedia.id via Canva
Key Takeaways

Tesla stock is up 13% in the past month on a delivery beat, SpaceX merger talk, a Barclays upgrade and robotaxi news.

Much of the gain rests on a SpaceX deal that has no terms yet, while Tesla's third-quarter profit fell from a year ago.

Tesla's forward P/E is far above its five-year average, and consensus earnings through 2028 stay below what Tesla earned in 2022.

Buying more makes sense only once the two companies' special committees put a real premium on paper, and the Dallas Cybercab launch in November is the next marker.

Tesla (TSLA:NASDAQ) stock is up 13% in the past month, while the S&P 500 barely moved and the Nasdaq 100 slipped.

Most of that came from talk that SpaceX (SPCX:NASDAQ) will buy the company, and from robotaxi news that hasn't reached Tesla's earnings.

Deliveries got it started

Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles in the third quarter, it said before the open on Oct. 2: down 2% from a year ago, but up from the second quarter and well above the roughly 461,000 analysts expected.

Then the SpaceX talk took over

Barclays analyst Dan Levy sketched an all-stock deal, with SpaceX as the buyer, on Oct. 14. On SpaceX's Oct. 20 call, Elon Musk said both companies had formed special committees of independent directors to weigh a merger, and called one "a good idea."

On Oct. 26, Levy upgraded Tesla to Overweight and raised his target to $450 from $370. He cited the auto business, Megapacks and robotaxis, but the deal leads his case: "We believe the anticipated merger is now a key part of the Tesla bull case."

There are no terms yet. A Tesla vote would need a majority of all outstanding shares, a bar Musk himself called high, and the agenda for Tesla's Dec. 3 annual meeting carries no merger item.

In Levy's all-stock sketch, Tesla holders would be paid in SpaceX stock. SpaceX's third-quarter revenue jumped 161% to $14.6 billion, but Barclays, citing Bloomberg consensus, has it burning $17 billion of free cash flow in 2030 while Tesla brings in $12 billion.

TIKR tracks 45 analysts on Tesla. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Tesla, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Tesla's Analyst Ratings

The quarter itself was mixed

Tesla's own third-quarter report, out after the close on Oct. 21, was less exciting. Revenue was flat at $28.05 billion. GAAP net income fell to $787 million from $1.37 billion, and free cash flow to $1.53 billion from $3.99 billion.

US equity futures were tracking in the red on Thursday as traders await a key inflation report and the latest financial results of e-commerce giant Amazon.com (AMZN).

The S&P 500 decreased 0.3% and the Nasdaq 100 declined 1.1% in premarket activity, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 0.2%. Wall Street finished Wednesday trading higher, with the Nasdaq Composite and the S&P 500 extending their winning streak to a third consecutive session.

The personal income and outlays report for September is scheduled to be released at 8:30 am ET. The report includes the personal consumption expenditure price index, the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation metric, as well as data on consumer spending.

Data are expected to show that PCE increased 0.5% sequentially and 3.6% annually last month, according to a Bloomberg-compiled consensus.

Treasury yields were down early Thursday, with the two-year rate retreating 5.4 basis points to 4.68% and the 10-year rate off 5 basis points to nearly 5%.

The Fed held its policy rate steady on Wednesday in a divided decision as the central bank preferred to wait for fresh data on inflation before deciding its next move. Chair Kevin Warsh also announced a reduction in the number of rate-setting meetings from the current eight annually to devote more time to discussions on monetary policy strategy.

"While the recent acceleration in inflation should be more than enough to justify firmer policy near term, the majority of Fed officials seemingly support a more patient approach to any further rate adjustments," Stifel Economics Chief Economist Lindsey Piegza said in a note emailed to MT Newswires on Wednesday.

Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissented with the majority, preferring a 25-basis-point rate hike, the Federal Open Market Committee said in its statement.

Amazon is expected to release its latest financial results after the markets close. The consensus on FactSet is for the company to post per-share earnings of $1.97 and revenue of $202.22 billion for the September quarter.

Shares of Microsoft (MSFT) rose 3% pre-bell after the company reported stronger-than-expected fiscal first-quarter results. Alphabet's (GOOG, GOOGL) class A and C shares dropped 9.8% and 10%, respectively, as the Google parent posted an unexpected year-over-year decrease in its third-quarter earnings.

Eli Lilly (LLY), Mastercard (MA), Merck (MRK), Caterpillar (CAT), Anheuser-Busch Inbev (BUD), Bristol-Myers Squibb (BMY), L3Harris Technologies (LHX), D.R. Horton (DHI), Restaurant Brands International (QSR) and Hershey (HSY) post their earnings before the bell, among others.

Intel (INTC), Sandisk (SNDK), Starbucks (SBUX), Stryker (SYK), Roblox (RBLX) and Reddit (RDDT) are due to announce their results after the markets close.

West Texas Intermediate crude oil fell 1.3% to $101.42 a barrel, while Brent ticked down 1% to $114.19 a barrel.

Vice President JD Vance has reportedly sent a letter to the secretary of Iran's supreme national security council, Mohsen Rezaei, at the direction of President Donald Trump, to resume peace negotiations, The Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday, citing US officials and people familiar with the matter.

Qatar has also presented Iran a new proposal to end the Middle East war, but a senior Iranian official rejected the offer as unacceptable, Reuters reported.

Thursday's economic calendar also has the advance estimate for the third-quarter gross domestic product, along with the weekly jobless claims bulletin.

OCTOBER 29, 2026 AT 06:14 PM GMT

Alphabet Stock Turns Negative for 2026

Shares of Alphabet were trading at levels not seen since April after the Google parent missed expectations with its third-quarter results.

The company late Wednesday reported earnings per share of $2.12 on revenue of $127.58 billion. Analysts surveyed by Visible Alpha had called for EPS of $2.94 on revenue of $127.89 billion. While cloud revenues roughly doubled to $30.7 billion, ahead of projections, search and advertising revenues fell short.

The results are fueling worries about the company's ability to generate enough revenue from its new AI products to justify its massive investments in data centers and AI hardware.

Coming into today's session, Alphabet shares had gained 4% since the start of the year, lagging the S&P 500's 13% gain over the period. Today, they're down more than 12%, and back in the red for 2026.

—Aaron McDade

OCTOBER 29, 2026 AT 06:14 PM GMT

Nvidia-Backed Marvell, Lumentum Could Be Nearing Deal

Chip designer Marvell Technology and optical components maker Lumentum could be moving closer to a merger.

Shares of Marvell Technology were down more than 11% in recent trading, while Lumentum climbed 2.5%, after Bloomberg reported that Marvell is in advanced talks to buy Lumentum. An announcement could come as soon as next week, according to the report. Lumentum and Marvell did not respond to Investopedia's requests for comment in time for publication.

A deal would give Marvell, which buys lasers from Lumentum, more direct access to a major supplier. It would also bring together two AI investor favorites, as strong demand has sent both companies' sales and stocks soaring this year.

Lumentum had a market capitalization of about $82.8 billion as of yesterday's close, while Marvell's is just over $220 billion. Shares of both companies were also boosted by a pair of $2 billion investments from Nvidia earlier this year.

Marvell recently hiked its long-term sales targets on booming data center demand. Earlier this month, Lumentum's CEO said the company is sold out of its production capacity through early 2029 for its optical networking products.

Marvell shares were up roughly 200% for the year through Wednesday's close, while Lumentum shares have surged 150%.

—Aaron McDade

OCTOBER 29, 2026 AT 12:02 PM GMT

Here's How Much Intel Stock Is Expected to Move After Earnings

Intel is set to report earnings after the closing bell today, with traders looking for a sizable swing in the chipmaker's stock.

Current options pricing indicates Intel (INTC) is seen swinging up to about 8% by the end of the week. A move of that size from Wednesday's close could lift the shares as high as $103, or drag them below $88.

Intel shares are up roughly 160% for the year, but have pulled back from their June record in recent months. Solid results driven by AI demand sent the stock surging earlier this year, but worries about the sustainability of client spending and Intel's fundraising plans have pressured shares more recently.

title: Small-Cap Stocks Just Did Something They Haven't Done Since 2018. Is It Finally Time to Buy?
detail:
Small-Cap Stocks Just Did Something They Haven't Done Since 2018. Is It Finally Time to Buy?
David Dierking, The Motley Fool
Wed, October 28, 2026 at 10:35 PM EDT 5 min read
^RUT
^GSPC
NVDA
^NDX
Trade NVIDIA on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

The Russell 2000 gained 2% during the week ended Oct. 23, ending six straight weekly declines. That was the small-cap index's longest losing streak since 2018. The rise also occurred during a week where the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC) and the Nasdaq 100 both fell.

That split is curious because we've seen this pattern before in response to changes in long-term Treasury yields. It could be caused by a couple of factors.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

One, small-caps tend to be more debt-heavy than large-caps and can experience a disproportionate benefit should rates fall. Two, we're starting to see investor concerns around artificial intelligence (AI) financing, net cash flows that are flipping negative, and rising credit risks.

This could be conditions swinging in favor of small-caps and the iShares Russell 2000 ETF (NYSEMKT: IWM) again.

Image source: Getty Images.
Tech spending triggers a flight to safety

After peaking at 5.36% in early October, the 10-year Treasury yield is back below 5%. Rates had been rising along with inflation, oil prices, and Fed expectations. But growing concerns about AI spending and the idea that some of the big tech names have overextended themselves have triggered a modest flight to safety that's brought yields back down.

That matters to small-caps that have borrowed significant sums to fund operations. Over the past two decades, State Street has found that small-caps have twice the sensitivity to Treasury yields as large-caps.

Valuation and earnings are the catalysts

One of the big things that has held small-caps back over the past few years has been a lack of earnings growth. Large-caps were doing great, but small-caps were offering little to no earnings improvement. That turned the group into laggards, leading them to trade at a significant discount to their large-cap peers.

Today, the earnings story has improved a lot. Small-cap earnings are expected to grow more than 20% year-over-year. But the Russell 2000 index still only trades at around 18 times earnings. That combination of fundamental improvement and valuation likely makes small-caps the better trade right now.

The risk that rates kill a small-cap rally

It's unlikely that the Fed will raise rates this week, but the futures market is still pricing in two or three more quarter-point hikes by mid-2027. With inflation and oil prices still high, the Iran war still raging, and soaring U.S. government debt, there's a strong case for why rates may need to move higher again to compensate.

The central bank held interest rates steady at 3.75% to 4% amid elevated inflation and a strong job market. The Federal Open Market Committee approved the following statement for release by a 10–2 vote.

Under Warsh's revamped framework, the FOMC will issue rate decisions at seven of its eight scheduled sessions in 2027, reserving one meeting exclusively for broad monetary policy strategy without issuing a formal rate statement. By 2028, the central bank plans to reduce its rate-setting votes to six per year, leaving two gatherings devoted entirely to strategic evaluations.

The FOMC on Wednesday left its federal funds rate target unchanged at 3.75-4.00% by a vote of 10-2, with two FOMC members (Cook and Hammack) dissenting and favoring a rate hike.

The market greeted the FOMC results as a bit dovish. Fed Chair Warsh reiterated the FOMC's intent to bring inflation back to target, saying the FOMC has "made clear our readiness to act as circumstances require, and we have shown our willingness to act."

However, some market participants apparently anticipate a more hands-off approach by the FOMC starting in 2027 as the Fed stretches out its rate-setting schedule. Fed Chair Warsh announced Wednesday that one of the FOMC's eight 2027 meetings will be non-voting and focus on broad policy strategy, meaning 2027 will have only seven voting meetings versus eight in 2026. In 2028, two meetings will be non-voting broad-strategy meetings, reducing rate-setting meetings to six.

The FOMC results could also be seen as a bit dovish because Warsh said financial conditions have tightened, with borrowing becoming more difficult, suggesting the Fed may face less pressure to raise interest rates.

Key Takeaways

Absci rose 12% today, Schrödinger 11% and Recursion 9%, and no company news explains any of the three moves.

Schrödinger's rally has the most business behind it, and Absci's rally is mostly about investors' appetite for risk.

In the second quarter of 2026, Absci had $0.3 million of revenue and burned $27.6 million of free cash flow. Management says its cash lasts into the second half of 2028.

Absci's third-quarter report on Nov. 12 is the next real test.

Absci (ABSI:NASDAQ) shares jumped 12% today. The company's only news was an 8 a.m. note saying it will attend some upcoming investor conferences.

It had plenty of company. Schrödinger (SDGR:NASDAQ) rose 11% and Recursion (RXRX:NASDAQ) gained 9%, while Twist Bioscience, Tempus AI and 10x Genomics rose 8% to 10%. The Nasdaq 100 and the small-cap Russell 2000 each rose 1%, so this looks like a risk-on day lifting the whole group.

Same rally, very different businesses

Schrödinger has real revenue to price: $255.9 million in 2025, up 23% from 2024. And even after a big run off February's lows, its forward price/sales multiple is close to its five-year average.

Schrödinger (SDGR): forward (NTM) price/sales, last 5 years (TIKR)

Today's jump takes it closer to 9x. That's a bit above its average, but nowhere near the nearly 27x it hit in 2021.

Recursion is further from paying its own way. Over the trailing 12 months it had $54.9 million of revenue and a $518.9 million net loss. It did raise $200 million at $3.25 a share on Oct. 15, so the cash is there for now.

Absci runs on sentiment

Absci is the furthest of the three from its fundamentals. It brought in $0.3 million of revenue in the second quarter of 2026. Even before today's jump, it was worth roughly eight times its cash and short-term investments. That cash rose sharply in the June quarter after a $100 million stock offering, which included a $40 million strategic investment from Eli Lilly…

Absci (ABSI): cash and short-term investments, $ millions, last 8 quarters (to June 30, 2026) (TIKR)

…and Absci has burned $26 million to $29 million of free cash flow in each of the past four quarters:

Absci (ABSI): free cash flow, $ millions, last 8 quarters (to June 30, 2026) (TIKR)

Management says its cash should fund operations into the second half of 2028, so there's no funding crunch coming soon. The valuation rests on ABS-201, which posted positive interim Phase 1 data in the HEADLINE trial this year.

Nov. 12 is the real test

My take: Schrödinger's rally has the most business behind it. Absci's rally is a bet on ABS-201 riding a risk-on day. A stock that jumps 12% on no news can give it back just as fast when the mood turns.
